Predicates:
FinancialAid(x) ::: x is provided financial aid.
ProveHardship(x) ::: x proves economic hardship.
SingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
FewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available.
LivingInSingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
FewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available.
Applying(x) ::: x is applying to take the GRE test.
CostGRE(c) ::: The cost of GRE is c dollars.
CheaperThan(c1, c2) ::: c1 is cheaper than c2.
ProvidesFinancialAid(x, y) ::: y provides financial aid to x.
Test(x) ::: x is a test.
GRE(x) ::: x is the GRE test.
Premises:
CostGRE(205) ∧ CheaperThan(205, 300) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test, which is cheaper than $300.
∀x (ProveHardship(x) → (SingleParentFamily(x) ∨ FewResources(x))) ::: Those proving economic hardship are either in single-parent families or have few resources.
LivingInSingleParentFamily(tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
FewResources(tom) ::: Tom has few resources available.
Applying(tom) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.
Conclusion:
¬∃x (Applying(x) ∧ FinancialAid(x)) ::: No one taking the GRE test has financial aid provided to them by something.
